panels.title: Fleet open (half or more replicas)
panels.description: egress:fleet_open, a Prometheus recording rule over every scraped replica's egress_consumer_breaker_state (infra/monitoring/rules.yml). Nothing reads it back; the EgressThirdPartyDown alert fires on it after 30s.

panels.title: Breaker state per replica
panels.description: egress_consumer_breaker_state, one line per instance. Each replica's breaker is entirely its own — this panel is where that shows: watch them open and close at different moments for the same incident, not together.

panels.title: Work queue depth, per consumer
panels.description: Messages ready plus in flight. Only climbs when the third party fails slowly enough to pin every consumer's in-flight slots (e.g. flaky-upstream's hang mode) — a fast failure dead-letters before a backlog can form. See the dead-letter panel for that case.

panels.title: Dead-letter queue depth, per consumer
panels.description: Messages that exhausted the broker's own delivery limit (x-delivery-limit, 3 attempts). Nothing here recovers them — that is a later article's problem.

panels.title: Calls to each dependency, by outcome
panels.description: egress_consumer_calls_total: ok, failed (counts toward tripping) or client_error (a 4xx other than 408/429 — dead-lettered at once, not counted). No 'open': an open breaker has no consumer, so nothing is rejected locally — the queue holds the work instead.

panels.title: Breaker trips
panels.description: sum(rate(egress_consumer_breaker_trips_total)) across all replicas. Each trip is one replica's own breaker opening — this counts events, not the disagreement between them; see the state-timeline panel for that.

panels.title: Active consumers on each work queue
panels.description: The broker's own count. With this breaker it is also the fleet's state: a replica whose breaker is open has cancelled its consumer, so the line steps down by one per open replica and back up as each half-opens (a half-open replica consumes with prefetch 1, so it counts). It should track --scale rmq-consumer=N only while every breaker is closed.

panels.title: Failed and refused calls, by dependency and reason
panels.description: egress_consumer_calls_total for outcome failed or client_error, by status: the HTTP status the third party answered with, or timeout / network when it never did. A 4xx other than 408 and 429 is a client_error: dead-lettered at once and not counted toward tripping. Everything else here counts.

panels.title: Wake tokens held by RabbitMQ — the open breakers
panels.description: rabbitmq_detailed_queue_messages for the delay chain (rmq.delay.level.NN), one line per level a token is waiting in. Level n holds a token for 2^n seconds, so a token in level 4 is a breaker that has been told to stay open 16s, and a token in level 16 would be an 18-hour hold. Each open breaker (one replica, one dependency) is exactly one token here; a closed fleet has none. Read alongside the panel to the left: consumers leave a work queue as tokens enter the chain.

panels.title: Parked queue depth, per consumer
panels.description: Messages redriven MAX_REDRIVES (5) times without succeeding — true poison, not just an outage. Should stay 0 for any incident this series injects; nonzero means something the third party will never accept.

panels.title: Redrives
panels.description: Dead-lettered messages the redrive moved back onto the work queue (moved) or parked as poison (parked). Nonzero only on the replica RabbitMQ elects active on the redrive-trigger queue.

panels.title: Probe permit — races lost, per second
panels.description: Half-open probes that found the one fleet-wide permit held by another replica: no call made, the message released, and the breaker held again at the same attempt.

panels.title: Concurrency limit per replica
panels.description: How many third-party calls each replica currently lets itself have open, learned from the third party's 429s (article 4): multiplied down when it says slow down, grown back one slot per limit's-worth of 200s. It starts at MAX_IN_FLIGHT and, against a third party that is merely full, settles near that replica's share of the third party's real capacity. Nothing moves it for a 5xx — that is the breaker's business.
